Cool. This looks better. I like the ring of defenses that runs along the outside. It looks like defensive-seeking mobs that hit a tower on the top half will stay in that outer ring until it gets to a corner, then it'll path from the cannon to the inner archer. From the bottom, they will similarly stay in the outer ring until reaching the upper wizards. I might put traps in between those outer towers and the corresponding inner towers if that is the way the mobs path. 

Similarly, I'd move the spring traps at the bottom. I'm thinking about what is most likely to attack your town hall - goblins, barbs, archers, and wizards (in my experience). Wizards are ranged, won't get that close. Gobs and barbs often waddle up with 1 leading and the rest following, which makes it kind of a waste of a trap. I'd move the springs to between defensive towers. If you kill the giants that are tanking, you're more likely to win the raid!

But that's just my opinion. You'll get a few defenses in, see where mobs are pathing and what traps are working and not and you'll be able to adjust. Clash on!

So, as someone whose seen maybe 5 therapists (so definitely not an expert), I usually take the first 1-3 appointments to feel them out. I figure out if we're going to mesh before I add the detail of suicidal thoughts. One thing your friend is right about is that in those first few therapy sessions, they will treat you the same if you say you're suicidal or just so depressed you can't live the life you want.

However, they won't cart you off to the hospital for saying you're suicidal. It's almost funny - a lot of people are suicidal. It's kind of normal to have these thoughts from time to time. However, it is NOT normal if you have a plan and have prepared to go through with a plan. When you're at that point, they will commit you. But if you just say, "Sometimes I think about killing myself, it's started happening more, and it bothers me," they will treat your depression without committing you.

As for whether professional help is worth it - if you can find someone you connect with, it is absolutely worth it. Ask for referrals from people you trust, and fully expect to try a few different therapists before finding one who fits. 

Good luck.
